en: The *Buddhabhāṣita-bodhisattvagati-sūtra*,
translated by the Śramaṇa Bai Fazang of the Western Jin Dynasty.
The Buddha was staying on Mount Śyena with five hundred bhikṣus, all of whom were arhats.
At dawn, they all donned their robes and took up their alms bowls, entering the city to seek food individually.

At that time, there was a wealthy elder in the city who was the foremost in the land; his residence was situated on high and dry ground, with excellent houses and towers, surrounded by walls seven layers deep and seven gates. His name was Dhanika.
Dhaniya-kātyāyana had a son named Śreṇika, who was sixteen years old.
Because Dhaniya-kātyāyana had passed away, Śreṇika lived alone with his mother.
When the Buddha arrived at Dhaniya-kātyāyana’s house seeking alms, [he encountered him there].
At that time, Śreṇika was staying inside at the third gate.
Seeing the Buddha approaching from afar, he was filled with joy and thought to himself:
"Why is this person so exceptionally handsome and beautiful beyond compare?"
"It is as beautiful as a bright moon-jewel, its radiance like that of the sun and moon, its color like refined gold, and as exquisite as the full moon on the fifteenth day.
At that time, the Buddha arrived and stood outside the gate.
He immediately ran inside and said to his mother:
"I saw a man coming; he was exceedingly handsome and peerless in all the world. Since my birth, I have never seen anyone like him. He is now standing outside the gate, seeking food."
Śreṇika said to his mother, "I shall give it to him.
His mother was extremely stingy and greedy and refused to give it; Śreṇika said to his mother:
"The people of the world are stingy and greedy, which is of no benefit to themselves; this is not the way of ordinary men, so you should give it to him.
His mother did not respond, so Śreṇika spoke to her again:
"This man surpasses all teachers in the world; giving to such a person is like a sick man finding a skilled physician."
Śreṇika said to his mother, "Please give it to him for my sake; this man is renowned throughout the world and is currently staying outside our gate.
His mother again refused to give it. Śreṇika spoke to his mother several more times, whereupon she became greatly incensed and said to Śreṇika:
"If you do not cease tormenting me, it will cause me great distress. This man has come for no reason other than food; he merely wishes to subdue you. What would a small child know?"
"If you do not stop your begging, you shall receive my beating with a staff before you will cease.

The Buddha, foreseeing that his mother was stingy and greedy, exercised his majestic spiritual power to illuminate through the seven layers of gates. When she beheld the Buddha’s radiance, her mind was immediately opened and liberated.
The deceased then returned to his mother’s side and said to her:
"A foolish person who does not know how to practice giving is like a blind man who has fallen into fire; it is solely because he is blind and sightless that he remains there."

People of the world merely sit idly in stinginess and greed; their minds harbor evil thoughts, their mouths utter evil words, and their bodies commit evil deeds. Such fools do not believe in the Buddha nor do they believe in the sutras; after death, they all enter the realms of hell, animals, or hungry ghosts.

If a person is not stingy or greedy, practicing virtue in body, speech, and mind, they will continuously receive its blessings for themselves. A wise person should provide food and drink as offerings to the Buddha; one should always associate with the wise, so that others may come to possess knowledge.
Śreṇika said to his mother:

"If you are unwilling to give it, then bring me my portion of today's meal yourself; I will not eat today. Bring my portion quickly out of compassion, for I fear that this person might abandon me, and such a person is difficult to encounter."

The mother again refused to give them; Śreṇika then went there himself to take the food and the fine, beautiful garments she was wearing. Carrying these out, he went before the Buddha, prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet, withdrew to stand with palms joined, and said to the Buddha:
"I offer all these garments and food that I possess, wishing to present them to the Buddha."
The Buddha remained silent and did not respond.
Śreṇika spoke to the Buddha again, saying:
"Now the Buddha is the father and mother of all people under heaven; you ought to deliver us."
"I grieve for you; may I receive this and thereby obtain its merit.
He said this three times.
The Buddha then accepted the deceased's robes and food, and the deceased was greatly rejoiced.
The Buddha said to Śreṇika:
"If you were to subdue all those who are stingy and greedy, and if today you were to give robes and food to the Buddha, you would cause yourself to obtain whatever you desire in your heart."
Śreṇika was greatly delighted and again addressed the Buddha, saying:

"In my heart, I do not wish to become Śakra, the King of the Second Heaven, the Trāyastriṃśa; nor do I wish for the Brahma Heaven, nor for the wealth and nobility of the world. My only wish is that my radiance and wisdom may be like those of the Buddha."
The Buddha said:
"Excellent! Whatever your heart desires, you shall obtain it all."
When Śakra, the King of Devas, heard Śreṇika’s words, he immediately stood behind the Buddha with palms joined. Śakra spoke to Śreṇika before the Buddha, saying:

“If one wishes to seek to become a Buddha, it is extremely difficult to attain; even after ten kalpas, a hundred kalpas, a thousand kalpas, ten thousand kalpas, or a hundred million kalpas, one may still not attain Buddhahood. Now, you have merely offered a small amount of food and clothing to the Buddha, yet you already wish to become a Buddha—this is impossible.”
Śakra spoke again to Śreṇika:

"If one were to give away the four treasures in quantities as vast as Mount Sumeru, and furthermore maintain a mind of loving-kindness toward all under heaven for a hundred thousand kalpas, a million kalpas, or ten million kalpas, one would still not yet be able to attain Buddhahood."
Śreṇika replied to Śākyamuni:
"It is like a master carpenter who enters the mountains with an axe to fell trees; he will surely seek out those that are straight and pleasing to his mind, and only then take them."
Śreṇika said to Śāriputra:
"I too have not offered even a single meal or a robe to the Buddha; yet, it is for this reason that I desire to become a Buddha.
I constantly maintain a virtuous mind and practice diligent contemplation without weariness; I shall certainly attain Buddhahood."
Śakra replied again to Śreṇika:
"If you wish to seek Buddhahood through arduous effort, it would be better to seek the status of a Brahmā or a Śakra.
Śreṇika replied again to Śakra:
"If I were to see Jambudvīpa entirely filled with fire rising up to the heavens, I would cast my body into it; yet I shall never cease in my quest to attain Buddhahood."
Śākyamuni replied:

"Even if Jambudvīpa were filled with fire, and within it there were people, domestic animals, and all kinds of crawling and wriggling creatures, you ought not to kill them. Yet you have turned your mind toward evil; you shall enter hell. How then can you become a Buddha?"
Śāriputra replied again:

"As for the people of the world and all classes of crawling and creeping insects, I entrust them all with a heart of loving-kindness to Maitreya Buddha; Maitreya Buddha shall naturally deliver and liberate them. As for me, my pursuit of the Buddha-way shall never cease."
Śreṇika spoke again to Śākyamuni, saying:
"Though the Brahmā King is honored, he too will ultimately return to impermanence; there is no one who escapes death.
Śākyamuni then joined his palms and replied to Śreṇika:
“You hold fast to your resolve; since you contemplate the desire to seek Buddhahood without ceasing, you too shall surely attain Buddhahood.
Śreṇika replied again to Śakra:
“Do not rely on the heavens to be arrogant, for there are those who surpass even you.”
Śreṇika said, "I shall hold a heart of loving-kindness and strive with unflagging diligence to seek Buddhahood; I will certainly attain the state of a Buddha.
Śakra then remained silent and had nothing further to say.
The Buddha then said to Śreṇika:

"Throughout your past and present lives, you have made offerings of food to sixty thousand Buddhas; your mind has always aspired to become a Buddha, and you have constantly maintained a virtuous heart in making offerings to the Buddhas."
The Buddha said to Śreṇika:
"After two hundred trillion kalpas, you shall no longer undergo rebirth among the denizens of hell, animals, or hungry ghosts.
The Buddha spoke again to Śreṇika:

“You have constantly maintained a mind of loving-kindness and made offerings to the Buddha; if you should later become a Golden Wheel-Turning King, ten billion minor kings shall all be subject to you. You shall govern the four continents and always travel by flight; all your deeds shall be upright, and at the end of your life, you shall be reborn in the Brahma Heaven and the Tuṣita Heaven.”

When your lifespan in heaven is exhausted, you shall descend again to be born as a Golden Wheel-Turning King; when that lifespan is exhausted, you shall ascend again to be born in the Brahma Heaven. After completing two hundred trillion kalpas of such ascending and descending, you shall become a Buddha named Sumerukalpa, delivering and liberating the people both above and below heaven.

When he was born and touched the ground, his radiance illuminated three thousand Mount Sumerus, reaching upward as far as the twenty-eighth heaven; the heavens and earth all shook violently, and both day and night were filled with light.

The people of that time all lived for seven thousand *koṭi* years; their bodies were two hundred zhang tall. There were twelve thousand cities, each four hundred and eighty li in size, and the gates of every city were adorned with carvings and inlaid with the seven treasures.
"When I become a Buddha, I shall assemble the śramaṇas twice to preach the sūtras.
During the first assembly for preaching the sūtras, six thousand koṭis of śramaṇas will all attain the path of arhatship;
during the second assembly for preaching the sūtras, four thousand koṭis of śramaṇas will all attain the path of arhatship."

At that time, among the people there were none who committed theft; men and women were all of one mind. There were no people who performed evil deeds, and the places of suffering in the various evil realms were all closed off. Furthermore, there were no mountains, forests, streams, or valleys; the earth was entirely level and even.

The people were free from disease and free from sorrow and suffering; all the people were happy, and each maintained their own household. Heaven rained three times daily, just enough to settle the dust. Whenever the people wished to deliberate on matters, they would all assemble together. In the summer months it was not excessively hot, and in the winter months it was not excessively cold, but remained perfectly temperate.

"The lecture hall where he teaches is named Nandita; if anyone makes offerings to the Buddha and the Arhats, they shall obtain whatever they seek—whether Buddhahood, Pratyekabuddhahood, or Arhatship."

The Buddha-way must be sought; the Buddha’s wisdom cannot be measured. The ten directions are infinite, and the Buddha’s wisdom is likewise without limit. The people of the world do not know from whence they come at birth, nor do they know to what path they go at death.
When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, Śreṇika, the bhikṣus, and Śakra, King of Devas, all paid homage to the Buddha.
This concludes the *Sutra on the Bodhisattva Śreṇika*.
